newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bluechips end mixed, wires crossed on Telecom.
newsitem.headline: NZ bluechips end mixed, wires crossed on Telecom.

text.p: * Telecom ends softer after largely in-line year results
* Brokers caution in-depth reaction in Telecom still to come
* Brierley Investments firmly bid after Thistle unit update

A widely-expected slowdown in underlying profit growth by New Zealand heavyweight Telecom prompted a dip in most bluechips on Wednesday but strong performances from a handful left closing indices mixed.
Telecom ended at NZ$6.63, down five cents from its last New Zealand close but unchanged from its overnight U.S. level, brokers noted.

The NZSE Top 40 index closed off 2.17 points at 2,300.99 while the Top 10 edged up 0.31 to 1,141.71, boosted by solid gains in Brierley Investments, up three cents to $1.34 in heavy volume, and brewer Lion Nathan, up five to
Brokers predicted a fuller reaction to Telecom's figures was likely to be seen in coming days as local and international analysts went over the numbers in detail.
Jim Patterson at First NZ Capital said there were few talking points in the market, despite the Telecom result. Total market turnover was disappointing at $33 million.
"The normalised Telecom earnings came out pretty much in line with what everyone was going for," he said.
"There was very little reaction to the results -- 400,000 shares (traded) through on the day on-market, which is very light," he said, noting some two-way trade after the numbers.
Patterson said Telecom's signal that it was now ready to start the second phase of its $1 billion share buy-back programme could restore confidence in turnover when it returned to the market.
Nigel Scott, head broker at Auckland-based BZW, said the market was still working out what exactly results from Telecom and, on Monday, Carter Holt Harvey meant for investors.

"I don't think either result has really changed people's current views on the stocks, on both Carters and Telecom. It's still very much on mid-ground waiting for the NZ economy to tick up and put a bit more emphasis on growth numbers," he said.
He noted Brierley's gains reflected broad buying interest.
"Brierley suddenly jumped out of bed this morning... there is a genuine amount of interest out there," Scott said.
Brokers noted that an upbeat Tuesday trading comment from Thistle Hotels, the newly-floated British based hotel group 46 percent owned by Brierley, had provoked interest.
Overall, however, the picture remained low-key and the tone dampened by the erosion of recent support that had been lent by falling interest rates and a softening of the dollar.
Comments by the Reserve Bank have caused renewed monetary tightening this week.
